results.bash53_output: `]]` -c/script/stdin: rc=2, stderr "bash: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token `]]'\nbash: -c: line 1: `]]'". `]]; echo after`: rc=2, no stdout (whole line rejected).
results.psh_output: `]]` -c/script/stdin: rc=127, stderr "psh: line 1: ]]: command not found". `]]; echo after`: rc=0, stdout "after" (psh keeps executing the rest of the line).
results.note: Reproduced in all three input modes at HEAD 6459f1a6. Divergence exactly as described: bash treats bare ]] as a reserved-word syntax error (rc 2) and rejects the whole line; psh lexes it as a word, resolves it as a command (rc 127) and continues. Not oracle drift — bash 5.3.15 matches bash_expected.

results.psh_output: With PSH_STRICT_ERRORS=1: full Python traceback ending "File psh/io_redirect/file_redirect.py, line 823, in _save_fd_high: return fcntl.fcntl(fd, fcntl.F_DUPFD, 10) / OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C int", process rc=1, f NOT created, `echo rc=$?` never runs. Without strict-errors: "psh: line 1: Python int too large to convert to C int", command rc=1, f not created. Same in -c/script/stdin.
results.note: Live at HEAD; the lexer still takes the >INT_MAX digit run as an fd (AST redirect.fd=2147483648) and the OverflowError escapes from file_redirect.py:823 (_save_fd_high). Under the suite-wide strict-errors setting this is now an INTERNAL DEFECT traceback rather than the swallowed exit-1 the report quoted. Side observation (not in the finding): for the in-range control 2147483647, psh reports "9: Bad file descriptor" while bash reports "2147483647: Bad file descriptor" -- psh names the wrong fd in the diagnostic.
